_.note: Notes shown under a setting's description, keyed by setting name. 'hidden' marks settings the in-game menu has no control for. A notes.json in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CoDTweaker adds to or overrides this list.

RendererWorkerCount.note: How many CPU threads the renderer uses for its job queue. -1 lets the game decide. Matching your number of physical performance cores is the usual tweak; too many threads on a hybrid CPU can add stutter.

VideoMemoryScaleMP.note: Share of video memory the game may use. Higher means less texture pop-in; too high stutters when Windows or other apps need VRAM.

DisableHWChangeDetection.note: Stops the game resetting graphics settings to its recommendation when it sees new hardware or a new driver. Useful once you have pinned your own values.

RecommendedSet.note: If this is false the game resets everything to its recommended settings at the next start. Leave it true.

LastSavedDriveType.note: What the game last decided about the drive it runs from; it warns when this says hdd.

SkipIntro.note: Skips the studio logos when the game starts.

SkipSeasonIntroVideo.note: Stops the season trailer playing at launch.

SkipSeasonVideo.note: Whether the season video is shown again after the first viewing.

EnableHUD.note: Turns the whole HUD off. Meant for screenshots and videos; leave it on to play.

ShowFPSCounter.note: The game's own frame counter in the corner.

CapFps.note: Master switch for the three frame-rate limits. They do nothing while this is false.

MaxFpsInGame.note: Frame cap in a match. A cap a few frames under the monitor's refresh rate keeps frame times even with G-Sync or FreeSync.
MaxFpsInGame.suggested: a few fps under your refresh rate

MaxFpsInMenu.note: Frame cap in menus. A low value keeps the GPU cool and quiet between matches.

MaxFpsOutOfFocus.note: Frame cap while the game window is in the background.

VSync.note: In-game vsync. With G-Sync or FreeSync the usual choice is off plus a frame cap.

VSyncInMenu.note: Vsync in menus only, so they don't run uncapped.

DisplayMode.note: Fullscreen has the lowest latency; borderless alt-tabs faster and keeps overlays working.

NvidiaReflex.note: Cuts input latency on NVIDIA cards. Boost also holds the GPU clock high, which costs power on a laptop.

AmdAntilag2.note: AMD's input-latency reduction, the counterpart of Reflex.

IntelXeLL.note: Intel's low-latency mode for Arc GPUs.

ResolutionMultiplier.note: Render resolution as a percentage of the window. Ignored while an upscaler such as DLSS picks the render resolution.

AbsoluteTargetResolution.note: Forces a fixed internal render resolution whatever the window size. 'none' lets the upscaler decide.

DynamicSceneResolution.note: Lowers the render resolution on the fly to hold the frame time set by the target.

DynamicSceneResolutionTarget.note: Frame time the dynamic resolution aims for, in milliseconds: 16.67 is 60 fps, 8.33 is 120 fps, 6.94 is 144 fps.

FocusedMode.note: Dims everything outside the centre of the screen.

ConstrainMouse.note: Keeps the mouse inside the game window; useful with two monitors in windowed modes.

DLSSPerfModeMP.note: DLSS quality tier. Higher tiers render more pixels before upscaling.

DLSSSharpnessMP.note: DLSS sharpening. 0 is none; above about 0.3 edges start to ring.

DLSSModelUI.note: TRANSFORMER is the newer, sharper DLSS model; CNN is the older one and a little cheaper.

DLSSFrameGeneration.note: DLSS Frame Generation on RTX 40 and 50 cards. Adds frames and some latency, so keep Reflex on. The game turns it off when the GPU or display doesn't qualify.

DLSSFrameGenerationmulti.note: How many frames DLSS generates per rendered frame (Multi Frame Generation, RTX 50). The game keeps two variants of this setting.

DLSSFrameGenerationDynamicMulti.note: Target frame rate when Multi Frame Generation is dynamic; the game picks the multiplier to reach it.

DLSSFrameGenerationmultiType.note: Fixed uses the multiplier as set; the dynamic modes pick it per frame to hit the target.

DxrMode.note: Ray tracing on or off, with its quality in the second variant. Expensive; the denoiser matters as much as the level.

DxrDenoiser.note: Which denoiser cleans up the ray-traced result. DLSS Ray Reconstruction is the best option on RTX cards.

GPUUploadHeaps.note: Uses Resizable BAR to send more data straight to VRAM when the board and driver support it.

EnableOfflineGameUpdater.note: Compiles shaders in the background instead of during play. Turning it off makes the first minutes of a session stutter.

OfflineGameUpdaterUsage.note: How much CPU the background shader compilation may take. maximum finishes fastest but makes the PC sluggish meanwhile.

ShaderQuality.note: Default is the full shader set; Medium and Low trade fidelity for frame rate.

SubdivisionLevel.note: Catmull-Clark mesh subdivision. 0 turns it off and frees GPU time with little visible loss.

StaticSunshadowClipmapResolution.note: Resolution of the static sun shadow map.

STLodSkip.note: Levels of detail to skip on some static geometry; higher means less detail and less GPU work.

SMAAFilmicAlphaStrength.note: Dampens SMAA's temporal history blend. Only matters when SMAA is the anti-aliasing technique.

DofWeaponDisable.note: Removes depth of field from the weapon even when depth of field is on.

DofWorldDisable.note: Removes depth of field from the world even when depth of field is on.

EnableVelocityBasedBlur.note: Radial blur that grows with your movement speed.

CinematicEmissive.note: Plays in-game cinematics on screens in the world.

CinematicQuality.note: Uses the lower-quality fallback movies when true.

ReflectionProbeHalfResolution.note: Renders reflection probes at half resolution to save GPU time.

ReflectionProbeRelighting.note: Update stages reflection probes get per frame. Lower is cheaper.

PersistentDamageLayer.note: Keeps bullet damage visible on surfaces. Costs a little VRAM.

VRS.note: Variable Rate Shading lowers shading detail where the eye won't notice, for a small frame-rate gain.

TextureQuality.note: 0 is the highest texture resolution, 3 the lowest.

TextureFilter.note: Anisotropic filtering. 16x costs almost nothing on current GPUs.

WorldStreamingQuality.note: How much of the world streams in at high detail. High wants a fast SSD.

GraphicsQuality.note: The preset the in-game menu shows. Changing single settings here does not update it.

GPUName.note: Which GPU the game uses on a machine with more than one. Pick the discrete card on a laptop.

SustainabilityPauseRendering.note: Stops rendering in the pause menu or when the window loses focus, to save power.

SustainabilityReduceQualityIdle.note: Lowers graphics quality after you have been idle for a while.

SustainabilityMenuSceneResolution.note: Lowers resolution in non-interactive scenes to save power.

BloodLimit.note: Limits how often blood effects can spawn; the interval sets the gap. Off means every hit draws blood.

BloodLimitInterval.note: Milliseconds between blood effects while Blood limit is on.

ShowBrass.note: Spent casings ejected from weapons. Off saves a little GPU time and visual noise.

MarksEntsPlayerOnly.note: Only your own bullets leave marks on entities.

InvalidCmdHintBlinkInterval.note: Blink rate of the 'can't do that' hint.

InvalidCmdHintDuration.note: How long the 'can't do that' hint stays up; 0 hides it.

CorpseLimit.note: Bodies kept on the ground at once. Lower values save CPU and GPU in busy fights.

CorpsesCullingThreshold.note: How aggressively distant bodies are culled.

AudioWantedChannelsNumber.note: Output channels requested from the audio device: 2 for stereo headphones, 6 or 8 for surround, 0 for the system default.

WindowsSonicEnable.note: Lets Windows' spatial sound (Windows Sonic, Dolby Atmos) process the game's audio instead of a plain 7.1 mix.

MicThreshold.note: Open-mic activation level. Raise it if the mic picks up keyboard noise.

WeaponCycleDelay.note: Minimum milliseconds between mouse-wheel weapon switches, for wheels that double-switch.

GamepadMenuScrollDelayFirst.note: Controller menu scrolling: delay before the first repeat.

GamepadMenuScrollDelayRestStart.note: Controller menu scrolling: repeat delay at the start.

GamepadMenuScrollDelayRestEnd.note: Controller menu scrolling: repeat delay once up to speed.

GamepadMenuScrollDelayRestAccel.note: Controller menu scrolling: how fast the repeat delay shrinks.

PitchSpeed.note: Maximum vertical look speed in degrees per second with a controller.

YawSpeed.note: Maximum horizontal look speed in degrees per second with a controller.

HTTPStreamLimitMBytes.note: Cap on on-demand texture streaming downloads, in MB, when the limit is on.

HTTPStreamUsageLimit.note: Turns the streaming download cap on.

HDRUseWindowsDisplayMapping.note: Takes the HDR brightness range from Windows 11 instead of the min and max values in the profile.

Fov.note: First-person field of view. Higher shows more but makes targets smaller; most PC players sit between 100 and 120.

ADSFovScaling.note: Keeps your field of view while aiming down sights. Off gives extra zoom on low-magnification optics.

MouseMonitorDistanceCoeff.note: How aim sensitivity scales with zoom. 1.333 is the classic monitor-distance match; 0 is relative.

MouseFilter.note: Averages mouse input over time. Adds latency.

Sprint Assist Delay Gamepad.note: Milliseconds at full stick before sprint assist kicks in.

Sprint Assist Delay KBM.note: Milliseconds of movement before sprint assist kicks in.

TargetRefreshRate.note: Refresh-rate target the game assumes for some timing decisions.
